literal: In Emperor Taiwu's time, supervised all armies encamped south of the desert.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he commanded all armies camped south of the desert.

literal: Rouran memorialized and heard.
idiomatic: The Rouran sent memorials and kept watch.

literal: Su was upright and bright, good at controlling crowds, comforting officers and soldiers, always sharing their toil and rest.
idiomatic: Su was upright and bright, skilled at commanding men; he comforted officers and soldiers and always shared their hardships.

literal: Campaign against Helong, for merit advanced enfeoffment to prince.
idiomatic: On the campaign against Helong he was raised to prince for merit.

literal: Died, buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Su's younger brother Hun, from youth skilled at bow and horse, Taiwu praised him.
idiomatic: Su's younger brother Hun was skilled with bow and horse from youth; Taiwu praised him.

literal: When envoys came from all quarters, ordered Hun shoot three beasts, every shot hit; all present together regarded it as skilled.
idiomatic: When envoys arrived from all sides, Taiwu ordered Hun to shoot three beasts; every arrow struck, and all present admired him.

literal: When made Director of Palace Affairs, quite by pride and indulgence lost office, moved to Changshe, killed by someone.
idiomatic: As Director of Palace Affairs he grew proud and indulgent, lost his post, was moved to Changshe, and was murdered.

literal: Kudou, after Zhaocheng's death, Fu Luo because of his senior years forced relocation to Chang'an.
idiomatic: After Zhaocheng's death, Fu Luo, considering Kudou's seniority, forced him to Chang'an.

literal: Fu Jian honored him, taught letters and learning.
idiomatic: Fu Jian honored him and taught him letters.

literal: Because of chaos, followed Murong Yong eastward.
idiomatic: In the chaos he followed Murong Yong east.

literal: Yong made him Administrator of Xinxing.
idiomatic: Yong made him Administrator of Xinxing.

literal: After Liu Xian's defeat, sent younger brother Kangshan and others to welcome Kudou.
idiomatic: After Liu Xian's defeat he sent his younger brother Kangshan and others to welcome Kudou.

literal: Thereupon pressed the southern border; at this all tribes were disturbed.
idiomatic: Kudou then pressed the southern frontier and all the tribes were stirred.

literal: Daowu's attendants Yu Huan and others plotted to respond; co-conspirator Dan Magan informed the emperor.
idiomatic: Daowu's attendants Yu Huan and others plotted to join him; the conspirator Dan Magan informed the emperor.

literal: The emperor feared alarming people's hearts, hesitated and did not act.
idiomatic: Fearing to alarm the people, the emperor hesitated and did nothing.

literal: Three days later Huan because of the plot told his uncle-in-law Mu Chong.
idiomatic: Three days later Huan told his uncle-in-law Mu Chong of the plot.

literal: Again told, the emperor then executed Huan and five others; seven surnames including Mo Ti were all pardoned without inquiry.
idiomatic: When this too was reported, the emperor executed Huan and five others; seven clans including Mo Ti were all pardoned.

literal: The emperor feared internal trouble, then north crossed Yin Mountain, visited Helan tribe, sent An Tong and Changsun Man to gather troops from Murong Chui.
idiomatic: Fearing civil strife, he crossed Yin Mountain north to the Helan tribe and sent An Tong and Changsun Man to raise troops from Murong Chui.

literal: He Man fled to Kudou; An Tong by hidden route then reached Zhongshan.
idiomatic: He Man fled to Kudou; An Tong went by secret paths and reached Zhongshan.

literal: Murong Chui sent his son Helu with six thousand step and horse to follow.
idiomatic: Murong Chui sent his son Helu with six thousand infantry and cavalry to follow.

literal: An Tong together with Chui's envoy Lan He both returned, reached Niuchuan; Kudou's brother's son Yilie resisted them.
idiomatic: An Tong returned with Chui's envoy Lan He to Niuchuan, where Kudou's nephew Yilie blocked them.

literal: An Tong then hid in merchants' bags.
idiomatic: An Tong hid inside merchants' packs.

literal: By evening entered an empty well and escaped, still fled to Helu.
idiomatic: At dusk he slipped into an empty well, escaped, and rejoined Helu.

literal: The army had not yet arrived but gradually pressed forward against Herangan.
idiomatic: Before the relief army arrived, Kudou pressed Herangan.

literal: Herangan inwardly harbored heterodox intent, then for Kudou came to invade the northern region.
idiomatic: Herangan harbored treacherous intent and joined Kudou in attacking the north.

literal: All men were terrified, none had firm will.
idiomatic: Everyone was terrified; no one stood firm.

literal: Thereupon the northern region's great man Shusun Puluojie and various Wuhuan fled to Weichen.
idiomatic: The northern great man Shusun Puluojie and many Wuhuan fled to Weichen.

literal: Helu hearing this urgently sent An Tong, Zhu Tan and others.
idiomatic: Hearing this, Helu urgently sent An Tong, Zhu Tan, and others.

literal: Once they knew Helu's army was near, the crowd slightly settled.
idiomatic: When men knew Helu's army was near, the host grew somewhat steady.

literal: Daowu from Nushan visited Niuchuan; Kudou advanced encamping at Gaoliu.
idiomatic: Daowu came from Nushan to Niuchuan; Kudou advanced and camped at Gaoliu.

literal: Daowu again sent An Tong to Helu, thereby fixing a meeting date.
idiomatic: Daowu again sent An Tong to Helu to fix a rendezvous.

literal: An Tong returned; the emperor crossed Canhe, exited north of Dai, met Helu at Gaoliu.
idiomatic: An Tong returned; the emperor crossed Canhe, marched out of northern Dai, and met Helu at Gaoliu.

literal: Kudou driven to extremity, seeing flags fled running, then was killed by Weichen.
idiomatic: Kudou, driven to extremity, fled at sight of the banners and was killed by Weichen.

literal: The emperor fully collected his masses; Helu held the emperor separately returning to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: The emperor gathered Kudou's followers; Helu detained him and returned separately to Zhongshan.

literal: Discussion says: The Wei clan began from Youdu, founded the imperial enterprise.
idiomatic: The commentary says: The Wei house rose from Youdu and founded its empire.

literal: Duke of Shanggu and others branched like tree wood, scattered streams of heaven's moat.
idiomatic: The Duke of Shanggu and others branched like limbs of a tree, streams from heaven's moat.

literal: Some achievements entered statecraft, greatly opening territory;
idiomatic: Some aided statecraft and greatly expanded the realm;

literal: some tracks matched fierce perversity, themselves bringing annihilation.
idiomatic: others walked paths of violence and brought ruin on themselves.

literal: Their fortune and calamity coming—only what men summon.
idiomatic: Fortune and disaster came only as men summoned them.

literal: As to Divine Martial not serving yellow canopy, high bowing to ten thousand chariots, righteousness moving neighboring states;
idiomatic: Divine Martial refused the yellow canopy and bowed to no throne, yet his righteousness moved neighboring states;

literal: rank ascending imperial line, Taibo and Yanling not enough to multiply.
idiomatic: his rank in the imperial line makes Taibo and Yanling seem slight.

literal: Gaoliang, heirs who yielded the state, Zina's fierce stalwart wind, some great position not yet added, some merit not redeeming crime;
idiomatic: Gaoliang yielded the realm; Zina bore fierce valor; some never reached the throne, some could not redeem their crimes;

literal: praising virtue plotting labor—the meaning is wanting.
idiomatic: to praise virtue and record labor for them—the meaning falls short.

literal: Songzi, spirit and trunk succeeding, voice and tracks both prominent;
idiomatic: Songzi's line carried spirit and stature together, fame and deed alike bright;

literal: Tianmu obtained the Way not—office exceeded his capacity.
idiomatic: Tianmu did not hold the Way—his office outran his measure.

literal: Holding fullness must regret, killing the body was fortune.
idiomatic: Those who hold fullness must repent; for some, death was mercy.

literal: Martial Guard father and son both generals, grand strategy at last seen valued, finally because of treachery discarded—not enough to regard.
idiomatic: The Martial Guard and his son were both generals; strategy at last won notice, yet treachery undid them—not worth dwelling on.

literal: Hejian, Fufeng, martial fierceness proclaimed bright—can the imperial sons be praised!
idiomatic: Hejian and Fufeng showed martial glory—among imperial sons they may be praised!

literal: Prince of Wei, heroic wind fierce and broad, repelling the foe seen weighty, plans not good, finally self-lost.
idiomatic: The Prince of Wei united heroic spirit with fierce force and was esteemed in battle, but unwise counsel brought about his own ruin.

literal: Prince of Qin, bodily measure broad grand, Chenliu daring spirit unmatched, lost body to strong enemy, ambition and strength not displayed—alas!
idiomatic: The Prince of Qin was broad in stature; Chenliu matched no one in daring, yet both died before strong foes and never showed their full strength—alas!

literal: Prince of Changshan, courage foremost among kin, rose and fell with Wei—also thereby superior!
idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan led the clan in courage and rose and fell with Wei—he too stands high!

literal: Prince of Yinping loyal and fierce, Puyin vessel and bearing, glory and favor both gathered—surely there was reason.
idiomatic: Yinping was loyal and fierce; Puyin had stature and grace; both won glory—there was cause.

literal: Piling coarse and fierce, Liaoxi narrow and unyielding, preserving body and keeping position—indeed also difficult.
idiomatic: Piling was coarse, Liaoxi obstinate; to keep body and post was hard enough.

literal: Fu Jian's strangling the true lord, Weichen's executing Kudou—rebellious sons treacherous ministers, surely also among the world's evils.
idiomatic: Fu Jian strangled the true heir; Weichen executed Kudou—rebellious sons and treacherous ministers belong among the world's great evils.
